objects.description: A client install bound to a subject, which proves itself by signing a nonce. Registering a new one is how a subject signs in again after a sign-out; a device's row is never deleted, so the record of what it was survives the door being shut.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, minted by the module.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: Who holds this device. Read server-side off the stored challenge when a session is minted, never taken from the client.

fields.name: public_key
fields.description: The Ed25519 key this device's answer to a challenge is verified against. Accepted as standard base64, raw base64url or hex. A device registered before the signature check was real carries a placeholder here and can no longer sign in, which is the intended posture.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the holder calls this handset, shown on the device list.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When this device was registered.

fields.name: signed_out_at
fields.description: When this device's life ended, or absent while it is live. A signed-out device may never challenge or verify again. Nullable rather than defaulted, because a zero instant reads as a sign-out and is not one.

fields.name: signed_out_by
fields.description: Which door ended this device: 'self' is the handset signing itself out, 'recovery' is a successful recovery ejecting every other handset. Never guessed — the screens that announce a sign-out open with this fact, and rendering a self-sign-out as a recovery alarms somebody who did it themselves.

objects.description: A short-lived secret a client must answer to prove control of a device or of a phone number. One use only: consuming it is what stops the same answer being replayed.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, minted by the module.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Which flow this challenge belongs to.

fields.name: device_id
fields.description: The device being proved, for a device challenge.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: The number being proved, for a phone or recovery challenge. Canonical E.164.

fields.name: secret
fields.description: The nonce a device signs, or the code a phone holder types back.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: Who this challenge is about. Never written to a caller who has not yet proved anything: a public door answering it lets an unauthenticated reader walk the id space and build a device-to-subject map.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: When this challenge stops being answerable.

fields.name: consumed
fields.description: Whether this challenge has already been spent.

objects.description: One phone number's consecutive-wrong-code state. Keyed on the number rather than on the challenge or the caller, so retrying from another device does not reset the count.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: The number the failures are counted against. Canonical E.164.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: How many consecutive wrong codes this number has produced.

fields.name: locked_until
fields.description: When this number stops being barred, or absent if it is not barred.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When this counter last moved.

objects.description: The standing link from a phone number to the subject that number reaches. Written on the verify path and not on the challenge path, so asking whether a number is known does not itself create a subject.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: The number. Canonical E.164.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: The subject this number reaches.

objects.description: An email-and-password credential for an operator console. The only stored secret this module holds, kept as an argon2id digest and never as a password.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, minted by the module.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: Who this credential signs in as.

fields.name: email
fields.description: The normalised address this credential is found by. Unique, so one address is one credential.

fields.name: password_hash
fields.description: The argon2id digest of the password, in PHC string format. Never copied onto anything a route answers with.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When this credential was issued.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When it was last changed. Stamped by the store, never honoured from a caller.

fields.name: disabled_at
fields.description: When this credential stopped being usable, or absent while it works.

objects.description: One address's consecutive-wrong-password state. Counted for an address with no credential exactly as for a real one, so a wrong password and an address nobody holds are indistinguishable from outside.

fields.name: email
fields.description: The normalised address the failures are counted against.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: How many consecutive wrong passwords this address has produced.

fields.name: locked_until
fields.description: When this address stops being barred, or absent if it is not barred.

objects.description: A subject's standing as checked by a human reviewer. A subject nobody has reviewed has no row, and reads back as unverified rather than as missing.

fields.name: subject_id
fields.description: Who was reviewed.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the review stands.

fields.name: note
fields.description: The reviewer's own words, shown beside the decision.

fields.name: full_name
fields.description: The name the subject gave, as checked.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: The number the subject gave, as checked.

fields.name: workflow_id
fields.description: The review process this decision came out of.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When this standing last changed. Stamped by the store, never honoured from a caller.

objects.description: One version of the key phone numbers are hashed under, so a stored number is a digest and not a number. Exactly one version is live at a time; a retired version keeps its row, because the digests naming it must still resolve and their staleness is only legible while the version they name is visibly retired.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The version operators say aloud: salt 1, salt 2. Rows elsewhere name this number, and comparing it against the live version is what makes a stale digest detectable.

fields.name: secret
fields.description: The raw key material. Opaque bytes, not text: this is the one value in the module that is a key rather than a record of one, and the only read of it returns a digest.

fields.name: set_at
fields.description: When this version began. An admin screen draws its age off this and nothing else.

fields.name: set_by
fields.description: Who set it, or absent for the first version, which provisioning writes before there is anybody to name.

fields.name: retired_at
fields.description: When this version stopped being live, or absent while it is live.

fields.name: retired_by
fields.description: Who retired it. Paired with the retirement instant: a version cannot be retired without naming who did it.
